paragraphs: Here's what I want you to hold onto, friend: Jesus is the great light Isaiah talked about, and He shows up right where the darkness is. Isaiah said, "the people living in darkness have seen a great light" (Matthew 4:16). Notice where that light lands: "Galilee of the Gentiles" (Matthew 4:15). I think that means the light doesn't wait for anybody to climb out of the dark first.

Then look at who He calls: fishermen with nets in their hands. He says, "Come, follow Me," and Simon Peter and Andrew leave their nets at once (Matthew 4:19-20). James and John leave the boat and their father right away (Matthew 4:22). I sat in a junk drawer for years thinking I was done, so believe me, being called is the BEST sound there is.

And the light doesn't stay in one spot, because Jesus goes throughout Galilee teaching, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness (Matthew 4:23), and crowds come from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea and beyond the Jordan (Matthew 4:25). So here's your takeaway, baker: Jesus comes to you where you are, and He calls you to follow Him. When you hear Him say "Come," what could you set down?
